title: Validate an email
instructorPromptText: Write a function that takes a string and returns True if it is a valid email address. A valid address has exactly one '@', at least one character before it, a domain with at least one '.', and no whitespace.

specGateDimensions.description: Where must the '.' in the domain appear — anywhere after the '@', strictly between two non-empty segments (so 'a@b.' and 'a@.b' are invalid), or is any '.' after the '@' sufficient?
specGateDimensions.rationale: The prompt says 'a domain with at least one dot' but does not specify whether leading/trailing dots in the domain count. Forcing commitment here prevents a very common drift.

specGateDimensions.description: Does 'no whitespace' mean only the space character, or all whitespace (tabs, newlines, etc.)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Students often check only ' ' in s and miss '\t' or '\n'; the spec should commit before coding.

specGateDimensions.description: What should the function return for an empty string, and what should happen if the input is not a string at all?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Empty input trivially fails every rule, but the student should commit to returning False rather than raising; non-string input forces a type contract.

specGateDimensions.description: The prompt requires 'at least one character before' the '@' — is there a symmetric requirement that the domain side be non-empty before the '.'?
specGateDimensions.rationale: The prompt is asymmetric (explicit about local part, silent about domain part before the dot). The student must notice the asymmetry and commit to a reading.

specGateDimensions.description: Are all characters other than whitespace and '@' acceptable on both sides, or is there an allowed-character restriction (letters, digits, dots, hyphens)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Real email validation restricts characters, but this prompt does not. Committing to 'any non-whitespace character is fine' prevents the student from silently over-engineering.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student checks for '@' with `'@' in s` instead of `s.count('@') == 1`, accepting 'a@@b.c' as valid
Student checks that '.' is somewhere in the string rather than specifically in the domain portion, so 'a.b@c' passes
Whitespace check uses `' ' in s` and misses tabs/newlines despite spec committing to 'all whitespace'
Plan describes sequential if-checks with early False returns; code uses a single boolean `and`-chain — coherent restructure
Plan describes manual scanning; code uses `s.split('@')` to destructure into local/domain parts — coherent simplification
Code calls `s.split('@')` and indexes `[1]` without first confirming exactly one '@', causing IndexError on inputs with no '@'
Uses `s.index('.')` on the whole string rather than on the domain substring, so the dot requirement is satisfied by a dot in the local part
